jobs.occupation: Supply Chain Launch Manager for global launch projects
jobs.description:
Would you like to help orchestrate the global launch of new products, representing our supply chain throughout the entire launch projects?

Join a global group of skilled supply chain professionals and follow new products from early development all the way to market – as your input will ensure that we deliver the best products to people with intimate healthcare needs.

“We play a key part in planning and executing successful launches – and we are a valued voice in the process, allowing us to set a clear direction,” explains Head of Supply Chain Launch, Global Supply Chain Management, Daniel Arildsen.

Join Our Highly Experienced Launch Department

Together, we are 7 colleagues, responsible for supply chain activities related to bringing new and innovative products to market within Chronic Care and Wound Care products. A good part of our time, we spend working with our factories in Hungary, Costa Rica, and soon Portugal.

“As we are each dedicated to different projects, discussing what we’ve learned with each other is very important to us. And we’ll be there to make sure you get to ease into the position,” says Daniel.

Ensure that supply chain is covered in every project

As part of the Coloplast global supply chain, you will find yourself in the middle of a web of stakeholders working towards launching new Chronic Care and Wound Care products. Here, you will be dedicated to specific projects, acting as supply chain lead or subject matter expert, representing the voice of supply chain and making sure supply chain is on track for launch.

Specifically, you will be the subject matter expert from supply chain, staying up to date on project progression. Moreover, you will plan the launch and make sure that systems, manufacturing, stock levels, etc. are ready for launch. And when you meet a bump in the road, you will figure out solutions with the project team.

From early project development until post-launch, you will:

• Influence project decisions and direction early, to avoid supply chain risks

• Drive the supply chain plan with manufacturing sites, balancing project deliverables and commercial considerations to launch on time

• Produce launch scenarios in collaboration with other departments and ensure alignment with the rest of the organization

• Coordinate activities at our production sites and flag supply chain risks

• Make sure systems, such as planning, base data and distribution, are ready for launch

• Follow up on delivery performance of newly launched items after launch

Your work may take you traveling roughly 2 weeks per year, primarily to our factory in Hungary. However, you will have a say on how the trips are planned, so they will fit with the rest of your life.

Supply Chain Knowledge And Stakeholder Management Skills

In this role, you must be able to work cross-functionally, using your good stakeholder management skills to incorporate a wide range of input from across the business. Also, you can work with limited supervision in your projects, representing the voice of supply chain, making decisions, and setting a direction for your area.

Finally, we imagine that you:

• Have a degree in supply chain or engineering

• Have some experience, either within supply chain or logistics and a good conception of production processes

• Possibly have some experience working in projects, allowing you to consider both commercial and supply chain perspectives

• Are good at Excel and at adapting to new systems

• Are fluent in English

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position, please reach out to Head of Supply Chain Launch,

Global Supply Chain Management, Daniel Arildsen on DKDAAR@coloplast.com. We will take candidates into the recruitment process continuously, so do not hesitate to apply. This position will remain open until a suitable candidate has been found.

_Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

__Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. We therefore encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religious belief or physical ability.

__Visit us on Coloplast.com.

__Watch the film. Follow us on LinkedIn.

What does it take to turn great science and technology into strong commercial execution? It takes people who understand the value, know how to communicate it, and have the confidence and skills to engage customers effectively. As our new Commercial Training Lead, you’ll play a key role in making that happen.

You’ll own and develop our approach to commercial training across our global sales organization, distributors, and strategic MS vendor partners. Working closely with Sales, Marketing, Market Development, Applications, and R&D, you’ll translate expertise into scalable training that strengthens commercial capabilities and prepares our teams and partners for what’s next. From value selling and product training to certification and new product launches, you’ll have significant opportunity to shape the role and make an impact. The role is based at our HQ in Odense and will report directly to our Chief Commercial Officer,

If this sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

What we do

Evosep aims to improve quality of life and patient care by radically innovating protein-based clinical diagnostics. Making sample preparation and separation before MS analysis 10 times faster and 100 times more robust will enable truly large cohort studies for biomarker validation and provide the foundation for precision medicine.

Key tasks and responsibilities

Training Strategy & Curriculum

• Own the global commercial training strategy, roadmap and curriculum.

• Build a scalable model combining live training, digital learning, coaching and certification.

• Establish a central repository and LMS for training content.

Distributor & MS Vendor Enablement

• Own onboarding, training and certification for distributors and strategic MS vendor teams.

• Equip partners with Evosep value proposition, differentiation and joint customer messaging.

• Partner with Distributor Leader and Market Development to close capability gaps.

Product, Application & NPI Enablement

• Translate product, technology and application knowledge into compelling commercial training.

• Own the NPI training workstream, ensuring sales readiness before launch.

• Partner with Product Development, R&D, Marketing and Application for consistent positioning.

Sales Capability

• Develop training in value selling, sales methodology, qualification and negotiation.

• Support Sales Leaders with coaching tools and capability development.

• Identify gaps through field feedback and commercial performance.

Effectiveness & Continuous Improvement

• Measure training impact using commercial KPIs, win/loss insights and field feedback.

• Track success metrics: time-to-productivity, certification, adoption, funnel progression and sales performance.

Qualifications

Your most important qualification is your personality! We care about hiring people who we believe can thrive and develop at Evosep. Our team is diverse, but a positive can-do attitude and the desire to be part of something bigger than yourself are common characteristics for the entire team.

For this role, we also imagine you bring:

• A background in commercial training, sales enablement or sales/application roles in life science, instrumentation or proteomics.

• A track record of scaling training across direct and distributor/partner channels.

• Experience supporting product launches with Marketing, Product and R&D.

• The ability to turn complex technology into clear, customer-value-led training.

• Strong skills in value selling, coaching and certification design.

• Skilled with LMS and digital tools to measure training impact.

• Excellent communication skills in a global, multicultural setting.

• A structured hands-on builder mindset to both design and execute.

• The ability to influence sales teams and partners without formal authority.

• A curious and outcome-focused mindset.

What We Offer

• A team of passionate, ambitious, and supportive colleagues with a can-do mentality and a strong belief in our ability to make a real difference through what we do.

• An innovative, open, and dynamic culture where we continuously learn, improve, and develop.

• The opportunity to join a rapidly growing life sciences company and contribute to solutions aimed at improving quality of life and patient care.

• A competitive benefits package and lunch arrangement.

• Flexible working hours and work-life balance.

• New, modern office facilities in Odense.

• And the list goes on. Learn more about us on Evosep Careers.

Does This Position Sound Like A Match?

Hit the apply button below to apply for the position. We are looking forward to hearing from you!

What Happens After I Send My Application?

We are looking for someone who can join our team as soon as possible. We will conduct interviews continuously and we reserve the right to close the job advert as soon as the position has been filled, so do not hesitate to send us an application. jobs.occupation: Maersk Air Cargo seeks a CAMO Base Maintenance Planner and Techrep
jobs.description:
Opportunity

At Maersk Air Cargo, we’re proud to play an important role in Maersk’s ambition to deliver truly integrated global logistics. Our aviation operation brings together specialist expertise, teamwork and a strong commitment to safe and reliable operations. We are now looking for a CAMO Base Maintenance Planner & Technical Representative to join our team and contribute to the continued development and success of our air cargo operation.

**About the role

**This is a hands-on role combining detailed base maintenance planning with the opportunity to represent CAMO on site during scheduled maintenance inputs. You will take ownership of assigned base maintenance events, including C-Checks, coordinating the work scope, materials and technical requirements before acting as the key CAMO interface with the contracted Part-145 maintenance organisation during the maintenance input. It’s an opportunity to work across the complete base-maintenance lifecycle rather than focusing purely on planning.

Flexibility to travel extensively is essential, with approximately 40–60 travel days per year, typically in periods of 2–5 weeks at a time, depending on the base maintenance schedule. Travel requirements may increase as the fleet grows. This role would particularly suit an experienced aircraft maintenance technician looking to transition from a hands-on, shift-based environment into a CAMO/office-based position, while remaining closely connected to aircraft maintenance activities.

What you’ll be doing

**Base maintenance planning & preparation

**You will:

• Plan and prepare assigned base maintenance inputs and the associated work package.

• Ensure scheduled tasks, ADs, EOs, inspections, modifications and other approved requirements are included.

• Coordinate material, component, rotable and modification-kit availability with Logistics.

• Align technical scope, schedule and readiness with Engineering, MCC, Technical Records and the selected MRO.

• Support task-card, maintenance-programme and planning-system improvements, including lessons learned.

Technical representation & on-site coordination

During assigned maintenance inputs, you will

• Act as the on-site CAMO Technical Representative and primary interface with the MRO during assigned checks.

• Monitor progress, findings, quality indicators, man-hour development, material status and schedule risks; report status to CAMO.

• Coordinate technical queries, additional work and findings; approve only within delegated authority and escalate when required.

• Monitor that the agreed maintenance scope is completed and appropriately documented by the contracted Part-145 organisation.

• Coordinate return-to-operation readiness with iOCC and relevant stakeholders, including deferred-item disposition where applicable.

• Ensure maintenance records, release documentation and system updates are received, reviewed, filed and followed through to closure.

**What we’re looking for

**Ideally, you will have:

• A minimum of three years’ relevant continuing-airworthiness knowledge and practical experience.

• Good working knowledge of EASA Part-CAMO and Part-145, with knowledge of Part-21.

• Understanding of MSG-3 principles, Aircraft Maintenance Programmes and scheduled maintenance planning.

• Experience working with aircraft technical manuals such as AMM, IPC, SRM, SSM, FIM, WDM and MEL, as applicable.

• Good understanding of work packages, task cards, maintenance records, ADs, EOs, modifications and repairs.

• Relevant aircraft-type general familiarisation and applicable company procedures, including CTS-1 and CTS-2.

• Strong communication, coordination and stakeholder-management skills in English.

• The ability to work independently and make sound decisions within delegated authority.

• Flexibility to travel for extended periods during assigned maintenance inputs.

• Experience or an AML relating to Boeing 767 or Boeing 777 aircraft would be advantageous.

If you’re looking for an opportunity to combine your technical maintenance experience with planning, coordination and technical representation in an international air cargo environment, we’d like to hear from you. Apply today!

Maersk is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we embrace different styles of thinking. Maersk is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applicants without regard to race, colour, gender, sex, age, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, marital status, sexual orientation, physical or mental disability, medical condition, pregnancy or parental leave, veteran status, gender identity, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. We will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with all legal requirements.

We are happy to support your need for any adjustments during the application and hiring process. If you need special assistance or an accommodation to use our website, apply for a position, or to perform a job, please contact us by emailing accommodationrequests@maersk.com.

Step into a team of passionate experts united by a common goal. With a strong technical foundation, a curious mindset and a passion for developing products that improve everyday life, you could be our next Product Manager in Sloped Roof Windows Category Management.

Meet your future team

You will join the Sloped Roof Windows Category team at our Head Office in Hørsholm. The team plays a key role in shaping the future of one of the most important product categories within the VELUX Group, connecting customer needs, technology, innovation and commercial priorities.

Working closely with Product Development, Engineering, Marketing, Innovation, Supply Chain and market stakeholders, you will help define where the portfolio should go next and what it will take to get there. Together, the team translates customer and market insights into product decisions that create value for customers and support the long-term success of the business.

The team is characterised by strong collaboration, deep expertise and a shared ambition to create solutions that improve life through daylight, fresh air and healthy indoor living.

What We Offer

This is an opportunity to work where customer needs, technical possibilities and business priorities meet. You will help shape products that influence the everyday lives of millions of people while contributing directly to how the VELUX Group responds to changing customer expectations, new technologies, sustainability requirements and emerging opportunities.

You will have the opportunity to explore important questions, challenge established approaches and bring ideas forward that strengthen both products and business performance. At the same time, you will be surrounded by experienced colleagues who value collaboration, learning and knowledge sharing.

More specifically your tasks will be to:

• Shape product roadmaps that connect category strategy with customer needs, technical possibilities and commercial ambitions

• Drive product lifecycle activities from early ideation and development through launch, optimisation and continuous improvement

• Partner closely with Product Development and Engineering to define product requirements, evaluate alternatives and shape future product solutions

• Build business cases and recommendations while creating alignment across functions and regions to support informed decisions and successful execution

You should expect some travel within Denmark and internationally to meet customers, installers, markets and development teams, and to understand how products perform in real-life applications.

What You Will Bring

Different professional journeys can lead to success in this role. Your experience matters, but your ability to navigate complexity, collaborate effectively and create momentum is equally important.

You are energised by challenges that do not come with obvious answers. You know how to explore opportunities, involve the right stakeholders and establish a clear way forward. Combining curiosity with ownership, you understand that strong results are created through trust, collaboration and clear direction.

Moreover, we expect that you:

• Have at least five years of experience within Product Management, Product Development, Engineering, Innovation Management or a comparable technical role

• Hold a relevant technical degree within Engineering, Product Design, Architecture, Building Technology or a related discipline

• Have experience working with technical products across their lifecycle and understand how customer needs, technical realities and business priorities come together to create successful products

• Build strong relationships, communicate complex topics clearly and create momentum through collaboration, influence and ownership

Experience from building materials, construction, fenestration or durable consumer products is an advantage, but not a requirement. We are equally interested in the perspective, curiosity and transferable experience you can bring from another technical industry.

Ready to apply?

Learn more about the VELUX Group online at www.velux.com where you can read more about working at our company and what to expect of our recruitment process.

We look forward to receiving your application and CV as soon as possible. We are conducting interviews on an ongoing basis until we have the right match.

All inquiries will be treated confidentially.

About VELUX

In the VELUX Group, we offer you a world of opportunities and the chance to create a bright future. From the forefront of the roof window category, we enable those who live, work and play under the roof transform their spaces and live a healthier everyday life with more daylight and fresh air.

The VELUX Group is an international, family-owned business with strong financial roots and each year we can create real impact by reinvesting in society, our employees and planet through our foundations. With 20 production companies in 12 countries and sales companies in 37 countries, our products are widely available. We employ around 12,000 people, and our company is headquartered in Denmark. Alongside the rest of our values, "courage" and "mutual respect" define our actions every day and how we wish to contribute to the world.

Equal Opportunity Employer

In the VELUX Group, we believe in fostering a diverse workplace for everyone to thrive, develop, and perform at their best, and where you feel welcome, respected, and valued. We are committed to providing equal opportunities for all - whether you are applying for a role or already a part of VELUX. That means we recruit, hire, train, and promote people based on their skills and potential without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, neurodiversity, disability, protected veteran status, national origin, sexual orientation or any other basis prohibited by applicable law.

We value diversity and strive to ensure that our employment decisions are fair and inclusive, focusing only on what truly matters: your qualifications and how you can contribute to our shared mission and success.

Do you have experience developing medical devices or other regulated products? Are you skilled at translating clinical and business needs into clear priorities for technical teams? Would you like to help develop innovative AI solutions that can improve patients’ lives?

Then your next career move may be as Product Owner for AI Development at Ambu.

AI Development at Ambu

You will join the Algorithms department within Software & Electronics in Ambu’s global R&D organization. The department develops advanced AI and algorithmic solutions for Ambu’s endoscopy products and includes specialists in deep learning, image processing, and data engineering.

You will be Product Owner for a cross-functional Agile team consisting of AI developers, data engineers, and a Test & Verification engineer. The team participates in Ambu’s Scaled Agile Release Train, ART, and collaborates closely with other teams and stakeholders.

The position is based in either Ballerup, Denmark, or Augsburg, Germany. You will report to Lee Lassen, AI Manager, who is part of the Algorithms leadership organization under the Head of Algorithms.

Your Role

As Product Owner, you will maximize the value delivered by the AI development team. You will translate product objectives, clinical needs, technical opportunities, and regulatory requirements into a clear and prioritized backlog.

You will work closely with Product Management, engineering managers, architects, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, project stakeholders, and other Product Owners across the ART.

**Your Main Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Own, prioritize, and maintain the team backlog in alignment with product priorities and ART objectives.

• Translate clinical, product, technical, quality, and regulatory needs into clear features, user stories, enablers, and acceptance criteria.

• Participate actively in PI Planning and support the definition and delivery of realistic, value-driven PI objectives.

• Coordinate priorities and dependencies with Product Management, architects, other Product Owners, Agile teams, and relevant stakeholders.

• Guide the cross-functional team through AI development activities spanning data preparation, model development, testing, verification, and product release.

• Monitor progress, risks, and dependencies while supporting design control, continuous improvement, and effective Agile ways of working.

jobs.description:
Copenhagen Business School invites applications for a postdoc position in the field of the intellectual history of corporate politics at the Department of Business Humanities and Law. The expected starting date is 1 May, 2027 or as agreed upon by consultation. The postdoc position is a non-tenured full-time position of 2 years, with the possibility of 1 additional year of teaching obligations.

The research will be conducted as part of the Independent Research Fund Denmark Sapere Aude Grant project Visions of corporate politics: Intellectual histories of the state-firm analogy. The project team will consist of the PI, one postdoc and one PhD.
Read more about the project here: https://dff.dk/en/our-funded-projects/meet-the-researchers/research-leaders/eksterne-personer-en/research-leaders-2025/mathias-hein-jessen/

The central objective of the research project is to analyze contemporary contestations over the state-firm boundary as well as mobilizations of analogies between state and firm in projecting political and economic visions. The project analyzes the constitution of the state-firm distinction as well as what it terms contemporary ‘visions of corporate politics’ represented by ideologically distinct answers to the crisis of liberal democracy which both contest the state-firm boundary and mobilize the state-firm analogy to legitimize their vision: On the one hand attempts to democratize or politicize the firm and on the other hand attempts to build political communities on principles of corporate governance. The postdoc project will focus on one of the two contemporary visions of corporate politics.

Examples of potential research topics: the democratization of the firm; democratic or economic planning; employee ownership; platform cooperativism or socialism; network states; gov-corps; start-up governments; freedom cities.

The research conducted will be team-based and oriented towards delivering on the project objectives. Taking the project framework into consideration, applicants are required to outline their reflections on how to approach the study.

The position is mainly in-place. The candidate should be able to be regularly present and attend meetings in Copenhagen.

For more information about the position, please contact PI of the project Associate Professor Mathias Hein Jessen (mhj.bhl@cbs.dk). 

Research environment
The Department of Business Humanities and Law is dedicated to an integrated approach to the contemporary challenges facing business and society drawing on the humanities, interdisciplinary social sciences, and law. The core research areas of the Department of Business Humanities and Law are organized into different research Units: Governance, Culture and Learning; Entrepreneurship, Ethics and Leadership; and CBS Law. Faculty within these groups have research backgrounds in areas of political science, sociology, philosophy, history, anthropology, law, theology, aesthetics, design and innovation, tourism and leisure management, cultural economics, leadership and strategy, pedagogic study, and other areas. What unites faculty in our department is an overriding concern for the organization of the human within its multiple environments: work, nature, economy, civil association, the state, and corporation. 

Teaching responsibilities of the Department comprise undergraduate and graduate teaching as well as teaching in post-experience and doctoral education. Some programs are taught in Danish, some in English.

Within the Department of Business Humanities and Law, the position will be located in the Governance, Culture and Learning Unit, an interdisciplinary research environment connecting governance studies at all levels of global society. 

Qualifications
The ideal candidate will have completed a PhD in intellectual history, history, political sociology, political theory or political philosophy. The candidate will be committed to an academic career, have the capabilities to conduct internationally recognized research and be able to communicate findings clearly. 

The assessment of the candidate will be based primarily on the following qualifications:

• Excellent academic track record
• Research within the history of political, economic or legal thought, political theory, or political philosophy.
• The ability and desire to work autonomously and as part of a team
• Excellent organizational and communication skills (both oral and written); proficiency in English is required
• Ability to engage with others in a way that reflects a collective commitment to diversity, equality, and inclusion. 
The application (see link below) must include a 3-5-page project description. The project description must include:

• a presentation of an original research question
• a description of the initial theoretical framework and method
• a presentation of the proposed material
• a work plan for the project
Application procedure
All applications must be sent via the electronic recruitment system, using the link below. The application must include:

A complete, numbered list of publications and work in progress (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review.

The application must include:

• Cover letter outlining motivation, fit, and qualifications
• A project description
• Transcripts (Master's and PhD) and a full CV
• A complete, numbered list of publications (indicating titles, co-authors, page numbers and year) with an * marking of the academic productions to be considered during the review. A maximum of 5 publications for review is allowed. Applicants are requested to prioritise their publications in relation to the field of this job advertisement.
• Copies of the publications marked with an *. Only publications written in English (or another specified principal language, according to research tradition) or one of the Scandinavian languages will be taken into consideration)
• Any relevant information indicating experience in research management, industry co-operation, and international cooperation.
• Documentation of pedagogical qualifications or related material.
Closing date: 15 December 2026

Recruitment procedure
The Recruitment Committee will shortlist a minimum of two applicants. If possible, five or more applicants will be shortlisted. The shortlisted applicants will be assessed by the Assessment Committee. All applicants will be notified of their status in the recruitment process shortly after the application deadline. The applicants selected for assessment will be notified about the composition of the Assessment Committee and later in the process about the result of the assessment. An appointment committee will invite a selection of qualified candidates to an interview. Once the recruitment process is completed each applicant will be notified of the outcome of their application.

Appointment

jobs.occupation: Chief Flight Instructor at GreyBird Pilot Academy - HQ located at Aarhus Airport, DK –  Ready to shape the future of pilot training? ✈️
jobs.description:
GreyBird Pilot Academy is more than a flight school. We are a fast-growing international business in an industry that never stands still – training the next generation of commercial pilots.

Since starting out in Aarhus in 2013, we have grown to seven bases across Europe – from Dublin in the west to Helsinki in the east. Our students fly under the Spanish sun and across European airspace. Today, more than 200 students are training to become commercial pilots with us, supported by over 40 flight instructors and a fleet of 12 Tecnam aircraft, with 13 more on the way.

This is where ambition becomes reality – where safety, people, technology, operations and training must all come together before the wheels leave the runway.

You have an aviation background and have instructed from the cockpit yourself. With us, you will join a highly skilled team with short decision-making lines and plenty of room to shape our development. We turn the dream of flying into a career – and you can help make that journey even better.

The role

The Chief Flight Instructor (CFI) is part of our ATO Core Team and holds overall responsibility for quality, standardisation and compliance in the flight and simulator training delivered by our flight instructors.

You are appointed by the Accountable Manager and report directly to the Head of Training, with whom you work closely to ensure consistent, high-quality training. The Head of Training may delegate tasks and authority to you within your area of responsibility.

Your key responsibilities include:

• 
Standardisation, supervision and training planning for the entire instructor team

• 
Developing and enforcing standard operating procedures for flight training

• 
Ensuring that all instructors hold valid licences, certificates and competencies

• 
Recruiting new instructors as well as guiding, mentoring and providing recurrent training for the existing team

• 
Assessing new bases as we expand into new countries

• 
Updating training materials and operations manuals on our in-house platform, SmartBird

• 
Taking part in ATO and management meetings, where you help set the direction for training

What we offer:

• 
Real decision-making authority over training quality and standards in a growing international organisation

• 
A direct reporting line to the Head of Training and close ties to management

• 
An established ATO with a clear, EASA-approved framework for the role

• 
Access to a modern and growing fleet

• 
An international working environment with colleagues and instructors from several countries

Requirements

The Chief Flight Instructor is a nominated post under EASA Part-ORA (ORA.ATO.210). In line with the regulation, the CFI must hold the highest pilot licence and at least one instructor certificate relevant to the courses the school offers. As GreyBird offers ATPL theory, several aircraft types and type rating-related training, we are looking for:

• 
CPL(A) or ATPL(A)

• 
Instructor certificate: FI(A)

• 
Additional instructor certificates such as CRI(A) and IRI(A) are considered an advantage

• 
A minimum of 1,000 hours as PIC, including at least 500 hours of instructional flying (industry practice is typically 1,500+ hours, and more experience counts in your favour)

• 
Ideally, you also have experience leading, standardising or developing other instructors

• 
Fluent English, spoken and written

How to apply

Ready to set the course for a role where you shape the standards for the next generation of pilots? Send us your application today – we look forward to hearing from you.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc and Assistant Professor Positions in Communications, Radar Systems, and Antenna Design
jobs.description:
Would you like to advance wireless connectivity and radar sensing for intelligent devices and autonomous systems? The section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for one or more Postdoc (2 years) and/or Assistant Professor positions in Communications, Signal Processing, Radar Systems, and Antenna Design. Join a growing research environment connecting electronic systems research with applications in robotics, drones, defence technology, and the Internet of Things (IoT). The preferred starting date is February 1, 2027.

 

Job Content

Your research will advance communications, signal processing, radar systems, and antenna design, with a focus on real-time wireless connectivity, physical-layer technologies, and antennas for intelligent devices, IoT systems, and edge computers. The scope spans 5G, mmWave, terahertz technologies, 6G and beyond, LoRa, software-defined radio, and integrated sensing, including communication protocols, modulation techniques, and antenna design and implementation. Applications include autonomous collaborative robotics, drone swarm communications, radar-based object detection and tracking, low-power radio sensor networks, and defence technology.

You will have the opportunity to connect your research with the section’s complementary expertise in FPGA and neuromorphic computing, edge AI, machine learning, sensing technologies, and energy harvesting. Working with academic colleagues and professional staff across SDU campuses, you will contribute to a collaborative research community and the development of academic programmes.

Postdoc: You will conduct research within the position’s scope, contribute to course planning, support teaching, and supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s students in relevant fields. You will also support the research team in developing applications for external funding.

Assistant Professor: You will develop and sustain a research agenda that strengthens or complements the section’s activities, secure external research funding, and publish in reputable journals and international conference proceedings. You will plan and teach Bachelor’s and Master’s-level courses in communications, radar and sensor technologies, and antenna theory and practice, while advising and mentoring students and supervising their research projects. You will also contribute to academic service at section and department levels, participate in professional activities and conferences locally, nationally, and internationally, and undertake other duties assigned by the Section Chair.

 

Required Qualifications

Applicants must hold a PhD degree in Electronics, Communications, or a closely related field. Your application must document the following qualifications:

• 
Research expertise relevant to the position in communications, signal processing, or antenna design.

• 
Demonstrated potential to teach Bachelor’s and Master’s-level courses at university level.

• 
For Assistant Professor applicants, pedagogical and subject-specific skills appropriate to the position’s teaching and research responsibilities.

International research experience gained in an environment other than the institution where the applicant completed their PhD will be considered an advantage. 

 

Workplace description 

The section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics brings together research in digital and high-frequency electronics, embedded systems, control, and communications. Using advanced reconfigurable computing and sensing technologies, we develop next-generation electronics and computing solutions for autonomous robots, drones, IoT, smart grids, and healthcare. This breadth creates opportunities to connect fundamental research with practical engineering challenges. 

Our research is organized into four complementary areas: 1) Infrastructure Inspection and Maintenance, 2) Bio-inspired Intelligent Systems, 3) High-Frequency Power Management, and 4) Radar Remote Sensing. The section is growing steadily and comprises 15 staff members, including professors, PhD students, and engineers, who contribute to research, industrial collaboration, and education. We play a central role in electrical engineering education in Odense, contributing to Bachelor’s and Master of Science programmes in Electronics Engineering. 

SDU’s Odense campus brings together six faculties, with a large university hospital soon to join the campus environment, creating opportunities for interdisciplinary research and a vibrant student life. Odense offers a culturally rich setting with a growing robotics community, attractive residential areas, and green spaces along the river through the city centre. 

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU.

 

Further information 

To learn more about the positions and research environment, please contact Professor Emad Samuel Malki Ebeid, Head of the Section of Digital and High-Frequency Electronics, at esme@sdu.dk. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

We welcome applications outlining how your expertise and research ambitions would contribute to the section. Please submit your application in English and include the following documents: 

• 
A motivation letter describing your interest in the position, relevant qualifications, and reasons for joining the section (maximum 2 pages).

• 
A detailed curriculum vitae, including contact information, research experience, teaching experience, computational skills, and other relevant qualifications.

• 
For Assistant Professor applicants: a Teaching Portfolio documenting your teaching qualifications and experience. 

• 
For Assistant Professor applicants: a research plan outlining your proposed research direction and plans for developing a research line, securing external funding, and building a research team. 

• 
For Postdoc applicants: a brief research plan outlining your proposed research focus, approach, and expected contributions during the two-year appointment, including its alignment with the position and the section’s activities. 

• 
PhD, Master’s and     Bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent (original     and an official English translation). 

• 
A list of publications, with the most relevant     publications highlighted.  

• 
Publications most relevant to the position. 

• 
Names and email addresses of up to three     researchers who can provide an informed reference at short notice.     Reference letters and documentation of other relevant qualifications may     also be included.  

• 
A statement/documentation     of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included. 

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

 

The application deadline is December 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

The appointments are temporary for an initial 2-year period (for the postdoc position) or 3-year period (for the assistant professor position). Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme.  

Employment as a postdoctoral fellow and assistant professor requires academic qualifications at a minimum of PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for either postdoc or assistant professor as described therein.

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

The Center for Industrial Software (CIS) at the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute, University of Southern Denmark, invites applications for a Research Assistant position. The position is based at SDU’s campus in Sønderborg and is available from March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is for 12 months.

The position is funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and is part of PREPARE — Pedagogical Alignment for Responsible AI in Software Engineering Education, a joint project between SDU and the IT University of Copenhagen (ITU).

CIS is a young but fast-growing unit whose research groups span cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, embedded systems, and software engineering. Our students and staff come from Denmark, the rest of the EU, and beyond, and our working language is English.

 

About the position

Generative AI has arrived in our classrooms faster than our pedagogy has adapted to it. Students increasingly delegate the very things we are trying to teach them — verification, trade-off reasoning, judgment, accountability — to tools whose reasoning they cannot inspect. Most institutional responses so far have been restrictions or isolated policies, and neither addresses the underlying problem. This project takes the opposite route: if AI is here to stay in software engineering practice, responsible AI use should be deliberately taught, practiced, and assessed.

This position sits where those ideas become things people can actually use. You will take responsibility for designing and creating content — reusable set of pedagogical modules that instructors can adopt without redesigning a whole course — and for the hands-on work of redesigning selected software engineering courses at SDU. The project’s research produces findings; this role turns them into activities, materials, rubrics, and guidance that survive contact with a real semester. Implementation is iterative rather than one-shot. Modules go into classrooms, evidence comes back through classroom interventions, surveys, artifact analysis, and educator feedback, and the next version is better for it. If you like building educational material and watching it improve under real use — and you would rather serve teaching than only write about it — this is a role with unusually visible results. Responsibility and opportunities

Concretely, you can expect to:

• 
Design and produce reusable pedagogical modules — guided scenarios, reflection and verification activities, assessment tasks, rubrics, and instructor guidance — that courses can adopt on demand.

• 
Redesign selected SE courses at SDU. Work with course responsibles and programme leaders to rework intended learning outcomes, activities, and assessment so that responsible AI use is explicitly taught and examined.

• 
Coordinate classroom deployments across semesters, keeping instructors supported and the logistics from eating the pedagogy.

• 
Gather and act on evidence. Administer surveys, analyze student artifacts (decision notes, verification evidence, reflections), collect structured educator feedback, and feed it into the next iteration.

• 
Document and release. Maintain the toolkit as open, well-documented material others can pick up after the project ends, and contribute to project reporting and publications.

 

Required scientific qualifications

• 
A master’s degree, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree, on Game Development and Learning Technology, Design and Interaction, Educational Technology, Media and Communication, or a closely related field. The degree must be completed before the starting date — this is a firm requirement.

Qualifications Required

• 
Demonstrated experience creating educational content — course materials, learning modules, exercises, assessment tasks, e-learning components, or training programmes — with examples you can show us. Please, share a link to your portfolio if available.

• 
An educational or pedagogical background, whether through your degree, formal training in teaching or learning design, or substantial practical experience.

• 
Excellent written and spoken Danish and English, and the ability to write clearly for two audiences at once: students and the instructors who will use your materials.

Personal competences

• 
Craft in making things others will use. You care whether an activity actually works in week seven of a busy semester, not only whether it reads well in a design document.

• 
A service orientation towards instructors. Course responsibles own their courses and have limited time. We value someone who makes adoption easy and earns agreement through evidence and patience rather than argument.

• 
Organized and self-directed. You will be coordinating deployments across courses at SDU and several semesters, and much of the scheduling discipline will rest with you.

• 
Comfort with iteration. The first version of a module will be wrong in interesting ways. Treating that as information rather than failure is most of the job.

• 
Integrity and care in working with students. You will be collecting data from people who are also being taught and assessed. That asymmetry has to be handled thoughtfully.

 

Workplace description 

The Center for Industrial Software (CIS) is part of the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute at SDU’s Faculty of Engineering. We are a young unit that has grown quickly, with close ties to industry in the region. We take our international workplace seriously.

You will be based at SDU’s campus in Sønderborg, sitting on the strait that separates the island of Als from the mainland. Sønderborg is a coastal town of around 27,000 in a municipality of 76,000, built around an 800-year-old castle and shaped by its position on the Danish–German border. It is small enough to cross by bike and rich enough in coastline, forest, and cultural life that people who come for a few years often stay longer. The international community is sizeable, thanks to the university and the global companies based nearby, and Copenhagen is a 35-minute flight or a direct train away. Two good starting points: VisitSønderborg for the area itself, and Hej Sønderborg, an English-language blog written for newcomers about living here.
